priorAttempt.category: Native guardian secondary-origin watchdog regression test

residualDiscardCase.selectionRule: Lowest-numbered completed development game with a candidate same-card-playable native discard lacking public Scrap text.
residualDiscardCase.interpretation: Playing required choosing a friendly creature for destruction; only actual destruction entitled its controller to steal up to two. The opponent had no amber. Both Play and Discard received one refill-slot credit. Avoiding the costly Play is supported by the public position.
residualDiscardCase.limitation: The margin over ending the turn reflects an approximate retention and refill valuation. One selected development decision does not establish optimality, the value of retaining the card, or the causes of other discards.

design.unit: Four games cross candidate seat and first player within each family, ordered deck pair and shuffle seed. Resample complete clean units within a family; aggregate point estimate only.
design.selectedScrapText: Presence of a nonempty Scrap effect list on the discarded card’s public spec or gained text boxes, including conditional abilities. This does not establish that Scrap resolved or that a choice was correct.

limitations: Previously seen fixed deck collection and two fresh confirmation seeds. Development and confirmation are analyzed separately.
Family intervals describe variation among these fixed four-game units. Decks recur across units.
Four selected historical observations diagnose action scoring. The bundle win rate cannot identify an individual change’s causal contribution.
Decision timing measures policy calls. Worker elapsed times overlap across workers.
